notification: The first MySQL 8.4.7 comparison measured nine-digit positive constants becoming BIGINT while the independent oracle expected INT. The production renderer preserved the exact numeric tokens. The original observations are retained.

materialization.rules: The threshold applies to unpadded positive integer literal terms in the signed 32-bit admission domain. Negative signed 32-bit literals stay INT. Legacy INT and BIGINT keep the measured signed display width. The existing CAST, Boolean, NULL, default, column order and value rules still apply.

witness.rule: Directly construct the specified ordered literals on all pinned releases. Compare exact storage, value, default and nullability. The new witness supplements every original authored, finite and seeded input.

preserves: Identical language acceptance, production rendering, release set, finite enumeration, original seed exploration, observation fields, allowed failures and fault controls.
